name: 8 Coil Shakti, both parietal lobes: burst stand-in for the caudate signal (slow alternation)
summary: Murphy's 8 Coil Shakti session over both parietal lobes with slow alternation (two coil pairs on each side take turns, one burst each), built with the project's amygdala-type burst in place of his caudate nucleus ('body') signal, which he publishes only by name. Murphy presents the caudate signal for body awareness and balance; the vendor reports tingling and sensations of movement for parietal sessions.
setting: Darkness and quiet (the vendor says effects during a session need darkness and silence); eyes closed, relaxed, without meditating or falling asleep; no meditation, mind machines or drugs at the same time.
schedule: Vendor's Shakti rules: at most every 72 h or once a week, never on consecutive days; a series of 3 or 6 sessions, then a 21-day break. Keep to it even though parietal thresholds are higher, and stay with parietal placement for the whole series.
notes: The vendor names a caudate nucleus signal and says 'This is not a well tested signal' ('Alternating Caudate Nucleus Signal'). It gives no shape, length, point duration or latency. Played here is the project's amygdala stand-in, the waveform of murphy-shakti-60min-bilateral-amygdala-slow (rising sweep, 6 to 30 Hz, 0.69 s, then 4 s of silence), so nothing played is specific to the caudate signal. Slow alternation is 'one switch after one instance of the signal': one burst plays on one pair of each side, the next 4.69 s later on the other (9.38 s per pair). The 30 min is the vendor's general session length. Coils sit on the strip the vendor places 'about an inch behind the topmost point on the head'. As in its photo, one channel drives the pair at the ends of the strip (CP1 and CP5, CP2 and CP6), the other the pair in its middle (CP3 and P3, CP4 and P4), which here sits front to back, not side by side. Each pair has one (+) and one (-) coil; site names and signs are the project's reading. Field strength: the vendor's 10 to 50 mG are gaussmeter readings at a coil (FAQ). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. At 1 uT that is about 56 uT at the coil face, 11 to 56 times the vendor's level. The vendor reports 'intense tingly sensations ... sensations of movement' with parietal sessions, naming both the caudate and the amygdaloid signal for them. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Other forms: murphy-shakti-caudate-parietal-bilateral-fast and murphy-shakti-caudate-parietal-left. The vendor says parietal thresholds are 'a bit higher' but asks users to keep to the normal schedules and not to switch between parietal and other placements. Not for people with epilepsy; stop at once if distressed.
